cells.tense: Right now, before any argument, something in you has already picked out what matters here.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: Take a decision or a worry that's still all fog and build the smallest structure that holds it — a day it happens, a page it lives on, one sentence saying what it is. Ten minutes, then stop.
cells.core:
You can tell what deserves attention before you could say why, and you don't need the whole road lit to take the step you're on. That part is steady. What it lacks is a container for the mess around it — good reading, no edges on the thing being read. So the form arrives late, if at all, and much of what you see stays uncarried.

Build the smallest structure that holds it this week. Take a decision or a worry that's still all fog, and put a frame around it: a day it happens, a page it lives on, one plain sentence about what it is. Then stop. Naming isn't deciding and it isn't explaining. It just gives your read somewhere to land, and what you see stops leaking out the sides.
cells.sheetLine: Something in you already knows what matters. Give it edges.

cells.tense: Ahead of you a decision waits, and you are trying to have the whole of it read before you move.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Move toward the thing you actually want — just face it, no reasons attached — while everything else stays unresolved. Not a plan, not a final answer. A direction you turn.
cells.core:
You can go far on partial light, and you don't need the whole road to know the next step — that gift isn't broken. What's bent is that you're reading toward a decision that hasn't arrived, gathering more so the ground will be solid before the move. The gathering has become the move. Nothing gets chosen, and you keep calling that thorough.

Move toward what you actually want instead. It's the thing whose loss would sting most, and you already carry it. Face it while the rest stays unresolved — not a plan, not a finished answer, just the direction your body turns. Most of what you've collected won't be needed for that; some will, and it'll come when the step asks. Choose, then let the choice be enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: More reading won't build the ground you're waiting for.

cells.tense: You arrived where you stand by running your own read past other people until it stopped sounding like yours.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Move through the fog on something uncertain without demanding the whole route — take what you can see and go, and notice what the going tells you. Ask nobody first whether it was right.
cells.core:
What you see, you've been handing to other people to confirm, and a read run past them that often stops landing by itself. So now the fog feels total, and the thing you see gets dressed up as a question for someone else. Nothing has left. It's been overruled by habit.

Move through the fog on something small without asking anyone first. Take what you can see and go; you don't need the whole route. Then watch what the going itself tells you. If it helps, picture how you'd want the thing to be a year from now, and keep that picture where the fog can't reach it. What you're after comes back through your own feet, not through another opinion.
cells.sheetLine: You see it. The checking is what's loud now.

cells.tense: Your reads keep proving accurate, and you keep filing the accuracy under luck or a hunch.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: After a choice goes well, give back what you're owed: say to yourself the one thing you'd seen before you moved. No modesty. Taking back what was already yours.
cells.core:
You read a room or a timing and act on it, then tell yourself the call came from nowhere. It didn't. The watching happened; only a name is missing from the page. You steer by it in decisions you believe are random, and by now your own accuracy surprises you.

Give back what's owed. After something goes well, say to yourself the one thing you'd seen before you moved — plainly, no waving it off. That's how your part in it comes home: not by taking more credit, but by pocketing what you already laid down. Do it a few times and the surprise fades. What's left is someone making calls they can watch themselves make.
cells.sheetLine: The accurate read is yours. You keep signing it someone else's.
